title: Install R

blocks.what_we_do:
Install R from [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/). Select your operating
system and its installation package. On Linux, follow CRAN's instructions for
your distribution; package installation may require an administrator.
blocks.why:
The R interpreter reads the commands in the notebooks. A package adds
functions to R; packages do not replace R itself.
blocks.you_need:
The system and processor identified at 0.1. On Apple Silicon use the ARM64
build; Intel Macs use the Intel build. Do not mix processor builds.
blocks.command:
Open R after installation and run:

```{r s0-2_r_version}
R.version.string
```

Terminal equivalent: `Rscript --version`. `--version` prints the installed
version without running an analysis. If the terminal cannot find Rscript but
RStudio can run R, use the R console; terminal PATH setup is not required here.
blocks.expected_result:
A line beginning `R version`. The version on your computer may differ from
the Windows validation environment, R 4.5.2. Ubuntu extraction was also tested
by the author using R 4.6.1.
blocks.troubleshooting:
If installation is blocked, ask the instructor or your institution's support
team for an approved installation. Do not change your system language.
blocks.quick_check:
What does the version command measure: the version of R or the version of PLINK?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>The version of R.</details>
blocks.files_created: The R installer creates software files outside this course project.
